slides.say: Six towns are connected so that every pair of towns has exactly one direct two-way bus line. How many bus lines are there?
So every two towns have one line between them, and the line goes both ways. That's a mutual action, like in the lesson.
at: every two towns have one line

slides.say: We'll solve it in two different ways. Let's start with the math way. We count as usual, in stages. A line leaves from one of the six towns.
It arrives at a different town, so five options.
Six times five is thirty. Thirty is one of the choices, choice number two. But careful, something is off.
We counted the line from A to B, and later the line from B to A. But a two-way line from A to B is the same line as from B to A.
So every line was counted twice. That's why thirty is a trap.
We divide by two. Thirty divided by two is fifteen bus lines.
[pause] Now a second way, with a drawing. Six points for the six towns, A to F.
From A, a line to each of the other five towns. Five lines.
From B, the line to A is already there. So B adds four new lines.
C adds three new lines, because its lines to A and B are already there.
D adds two, and E adds one. F has no new lines left.
Five plus four plus three plus two plus one is fifteen. The same fifteen lines.
Choice number one is our answer, and I'll see you in the next question.
at: Choice number one is our answer
